---
title: "Architecture Overview"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::rename, .quiet = TRUE)
```

## Class hierarchy

PKNCA uses four S3 classes: `PKNCAconc` and `PKNCAdose` feed `PKNCAdata`, and `pk.nca()` wraps the result into `PKNCAresults`:

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class PKNCAconc {
        data: data.frame
        formula: conc~time|groups
        subject: column name
        sparse: logical
        units: concu/amountu/timeu
        exclude / exclude_half.life / include_half.life
        lloq, time.nominal
        volume, duration (only if given)
    }
    class PKNCAdose {
        data: data.frame
        formula: dose~time|groups
        route: intravas./extravas.
        duration / rate
        units: doseu
        time.nominal
    }
    class PKNCAdata {
        conc: PKNCAconc
        dose: PKNCAdose
        intervals: data.frame
        impute: method string or column
        units: pknca_units_table()
        options: named list
        group_ref, grpid_cols
    }
    class PKNCAresults {
        result: data.frame incl. PPANMETH
        data: PKNCAdata
        exclude: column name
    }

    PKNCAconc --> PKNCAdata
    PKNCAdose --> PKNCAdata
    PKNCAdata --> PKNCAresults
```

## How a calculation runs

`PKNCAdata()` assembles the inputs and `pk.nca()` does the work. At a high level (function names are from `R/class-PKNCAdata.R` and `R/pk.calc.all.R`):

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["PKNCAdata()"] --> A1["Intervals: given, or generated per group by<br/>choose.auc.intervals() (auto.interval.method)"]
    A1 --> A2["set_intervals() / check.interval.specification()<br/>validate the intervals"]
    A2 --> A3["Units table: given, or pknca_units_table()"]
    A3 --> B["pk.nca()"]
    B --> B1["assert_intervals(); convert date-time<br/>times and intervals to numbers"]
    B1 --> B2["Overlay the object's options on a<br/>copy of PKNCA.options()"]
    B2 --> B3["Expand reference intervals for<br/>secondary parameters"]
    B3 --> B4["full_join_PKNCAdata(): split concentration,<br/>dose, and interval data by group"]
    B4 --> C["pk.nca.intervals(): one call per group"]
    C --> D["pk.nca.interval(): one call per interval;<br/>dense and sparse parameters in one pass"]
    D --> E["Gather results (dense, then sparse)"]
    E --> F["pk_nca_secondary(): parameters that<br/>read a reference interval"]
    F --> G["PKNCAresults()"]
```

Inside `pk.nca.interval()`, the requested parameters are expanded with their `depends`, put in dependency order, and calculated one at a time. For each parameter, the arguments of its calculation function are filled from the interval data, earlier results, constants, or the options (see [formalsmap](#formalsmap)); points named by `include_half.life`/`exclude_half.life` are applied before `half.life` is calculated; and the result's `exclude` and `"method"` attributes become the `exclude` and `PPANMETH` columns. A function that returns a data frame contributes one result row per column. The calculation functions themselves never see a `PKNCAdata` object, so they can be called directly (see [Utility Functions](../user/utilities.qmd)).

## The interval column system

The parameter registry is the core extensibility mechanism. Every NCA parameter is registered as an **interval column** via `add.interval.col()`.

```{r}
# Inspect registration for auclast
cols <- get.interval.cols()
str(cols[["auclast"]])
```

Each entry contains:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `FUN` | Name of the function that computes this parameter (character string, or `NA` for parameters populated by another function's multi-column result or calculated only by `FUN_sparse`) |
| `FUN_sparse` | Name of a sparse-PK estimator, or `NA` (≥ 0.13.0) |
| `values` | Allowed values in the interval column (typically `c(FALSE, TRUE)`) |
| `unit_type` | Unit category used for unit assignment and conversion |
| `pretty_name` | Human-readable name used in summary tables |
| `desc` | Human-readable description (40 characters or fewer for SDTM; longer warns) |
| `formalsmap` | Maps function arguments to interval/group/options data, other parameters, constants, or reference-interval values |
| `formalsmap_sparse` | The `formalsmap` for `FUN_sparse` (≥ 0.13.0) |
| `depends` | Character vector of parameters that must be computed first |
| `datatype` | Calculation type; only `"interval"` is currently supported |
| `pptestcd_cdisc` | CDISC PPTESTCD code: a string, a route-keyed list, or a dense/sparse list (≥ 0.13.0) |
| `pptest_cdisc` | CDISC PPTEST label, in the same forms (≥ 0.13.0) |
| `formula`, `formula_note` | LaTeX formula and note for documentation; `formula_note` is the `PPANMETH` fallback (≥ 0.13.0) |
| `tier`, `selection` | Classification for automatic interval selection (≥ 0.13.0) |

The registry has no `sparse` field (≥ 0.13.0): `add.interval.col(sparse = TRUE)` is retired and is an error. Whether a parameter needs sparse data is derived from the registration (a `FUN_sparse` and no `FUN`) and reported by `pknca_parameter_table()`, together with each parameter's concept, tier, and route and dosing contexts. After `pk.nca()` first uses an entry, it can also carry internal cached fields (`requires_*` and `arg_spec`) that are not part of the registration.

## formalsmap

`formalsmap` is how PKNCA passes the right data to each parameter function. Arguments can be sourced from these places:

| Source type | Example | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| Interval data | `conc`, `time`, `dose`, `time.dose`, `route` | Data for the current interval (times relative to the interval start) |
| Group data | `conc.group`, `time.group` | Data for the whole group |
| Sparse data (≥ 0.13.0) | `conc.sparse`, `time.sparse`, `subject` | The pooled individual samples (`NULL` for dense data) |
| Other parameters | `auc = "auclast"` | A previously computed NCA result |
| Interval bounds | `start`, `end` | The interval start/end times |
| Options | `options` | The full analysis options list |
| Constants (≥ 0.13.0) | `auc.type = I("AUCall")` | The value itself |
| Reference interval (≥ 0.13.0) | `auc = pknca_ref("auclast")` | A parameter's value in the reference interval; makes the parameter secondary |

Individual option names (e.g. `auc.method`) cannot be mapped through `formalsmap`; only the whole `options` list can, and parameter functions read specific settings from it via `PKNCA.choose.option()`.

## Writing a custom parameter

Registering a new parameter is a single `add.interval.col()` call that names the computing function; PKNCA then derives execution order from `depends`, assigns units from `unit_type`, and collects results automatically. A minimal toy registration:

```{r}
# Toy illustration: ratio of two built-in parameters
pk.calc.demo.ratio <- function(cmax, cmin) {
  cmax / cmin
}

add.interval.col(
  name        = "demo.ratio",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.demo.ratio",  # must be a character string, not the function object
  unit_type   = "unitless",
  pretty_name = "Demo ratio (Cmax/Cmin)",
  desc        = "Toy example: Cmax divided by Cmin",
  depends     = c("cmax", "cmin")
)

# The registry now contains it alongside the built-in parameters
str(get.interval.cols()[["demo.ratio"]])
```

For the full walkthrough — parameters computed from raw concentration-time data, constants, multi-output functions, parameters that read a reference interval, sparse-only parameters, and custom summary statistics — see the [Writing Custom Parameters chapter](../user/custom-parameters.qmd) and the package vignette [Writing PKNCA Parameter Functions](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v80-writing-parameter-functions.html).

## Options system

PKNCA's options are stored in a package-level environment; `PKNCA.options()` returns them as a named list. It is accessed in several ways:

```{r}
# 1. Read all options
PKNCA.options()

# 2. Read a specific option
PKNCA.options("min.hl.points")

# 3. Set globally — save the old value first so you can restore it
old_val <- PKNCA.options("min.hl.points")[[1]]
PKNCA.options(min.hl.points = 4)
PKNCA.options("min.hl.points")

# 4. Restore by passing the saved value as a named argument
PKNCA.options(min.hl.points = old_val)
PKNCA.options("min.hl.points")
```

> Prefer passing `options = list(...)` to `PKNCAdata()` over mutating global options. Global changes persist across analyses in the same session. At the start of each run, `pk.nca()` overlays the object's options on a copy of the global options and uses that copy for the calculations; the global options themselves are not modified. `PKNCA_options_defaults()` (≥ 0.13.0) returns the package defaults without resetting anything.

## Sparse PK

Sparse PK (one or two samples per subject, common in preclinical or pediatric studies) shares the dense code path (≥ 0.13.0):

- Set `sparse = TRUE` in `PKNCAconc()`.
- Each group reaches `pk.nca.interval()` with two representations of the same samples: the arithmetic-mean profile (as `conc`/`time`) and the pooled individual samples (as `conc.sparse`/`time.sparse`, with `subject`). Dense and sparse parameters are calculated in one pass.
- A parameter with a `FUN_sparse` (such as `auclast`, whose sparse estimator also returns `auclast_se` and `auclast_df`) is calculated from the pooled samples; one without falls back to `FUN` on the mean profile (half-life, for example). A parameter with `FUN = NA` and a `FUN_sparse` is sparse-only, and requesting it for dense data is an error.
- `pknca_parameter_table()$sparse` reports which parameters need sparse data.

For the full workflow, see the [Sparse NCA chapter](../user/sparse.qmd) and the vignette [Sparse NCA Calculations](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v04-sparse.html).

## Conditions and messages

Errors, warnings, and messages are signaled with `rlang` and carry classes named `pknca_error_*`, `pknca_warning_*`, and `pknca_message_*` (≥ 0.13.0), so code can catch them by class rather than by message text. Several older classes were renamed in 0.13.0 (for example, `pknca_conc_none` is now `pknca_warning_no_concentration`). Input validation uses `checkmate`. With `verbose = TRUE`, `pk.nca()` reports one "Starting PK NCA calculations." message (`pknca_message_pk_start`).

```{r}
# Catch a PKNCA error by its class
tryCatch(
  add.interval.col(name = "x_ref", FUN = "pk.calc.cmax", unit_type = "conc",
                   pretty_name = "x", desc = "Reserved name"),
  pknca_error_param_name_reserved = function(e) class(e)[1]
)
```

## Key functions

All of these are exported except where marked internal:

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get.interval.cols()` | Return full parameter registry |
| `pknca_parameter_table()` | Classification of every parameter (concept, tier, sparse, secondary, contexts) |
| `get.parameter.deps()` | Parameters calculated from a parameter, or with `recursive = TRUE` what it is calculated from |
| `PKNCA:::sort_interval_cols()` | Topological sort → execution order (internal, unexported) |
| `assert_intervals()` | Validate an interval specification against a `PKNCAdata` object |
| `pk.nca.interval()` | Compute all parameters for one interval/group; takes `conc.sparse`, `time.sparse`, `conc.sparse.group`, and `time.sparse.group` for sparse data (its `sparse` argument was removed in 0.13.0) |
| `pknca_units_table()` | Build unit assignment/conversion table |
| `PKNCA_impute_method_*()` | Built-in imputation methods (listed by `pknca_impute_methods()`) |
| `pk.calc.auc.last()` | Core AUC calculation; returns a `"method"` attribute |
| `pk.calc.half.life()` | λz regression with best-fit selection |
